lesson.title: Leaked email, safe password: what a data breach means for you
body: 1Password confirmed a security incident this week. The Verge reports customer names and email addresses leaked, but not passwords. That sounds harmless, but it isn't nothing.

A list of real names and emails, all known to use a password manager, is ideal material for phishing. Expect emails that look like they come from the company, warning you to 'verify your vault' or 'reset your account' via a link.

The defence is simple: never act on a link in a security email. Open the app or type the website address yourself. If there's a genuine problem, you'll see it there. Turning on two-factor authentication on your main email account adds a second lock if anything does get through.
You can check whether your email has appeared in known breaches with free services such as Have I Been Pwned, and change any password you've reused elsewhere.
lesson.takeaway: After a breach, the leak is rarely the danger. The follow-up phishing email is. Go direct, don't click.

m365.title: Assign a task with an @mention in a Word comment
m365.what: Instead of emailing 'can you check paragraph 3?', assign it inside the document. The person is notified by email and the comment shows who owns it.
try: Open a document saved in OneDrive or SharePoint in Word for the web or the Microsoft 365 desktop app.
Select the text you want looked at, then choose Review > New Comment.
Type @ followed by the person's name and pick them from the list.
Tick the 'Assign to' box that appears under the comment, then post it.
When it's done, they (or you) can resolve the comment so the task closes.

explainer.story: Energy bills to rise by 26% from January after gas prices surge
bullets: Ofgem's cap for a typical dual-fuel household on Direct Debit goes from £1,723 a year to about £2,166 for 1 January to 31 March 2027, a 26% jump.
The BBC says the rise follows a surge in wholesale gas prices. Ofgem resets the cap every three months to reflect those costs.
The cap limits unit rates and daily standing charges, not your total bill. Today's Direct Debit rates are 26.32p/kWh for electricity and 7.97p/kWh for gas.
explainer.why: Most households on standard tariffs will pay more from New Year. It also adds to the inflation pressure the Bank of England is weighing before its 17 December decision.
